title: add commandline runbook generator and contextual diagnostics to incident-bot
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: on-call engineers repeatedly ask for a compact, executable runbook that is generated from incident context (alerts, recent errors, and top traces). This PR adds a lightweight CLI and an incident-bot integration that synthesizes a short runbook (commands, prioritized checks, and escalation steps) and an optional contextual diagnostics payload. Key goals: 1) reduce time-to-first-action for pagers, 2) avoid noise by surfacing only high-confidence runbook steps, 3) keep sensitive traces private by opt-in sampling and obfuscation. What this PR includes: - incident-bot: new /runbook action that can be invoked via Slack or REST to generate a runbook based on the incident object. The generated runbook is markdown with actionable shell snippets and suggested queries. - oncall-cli: a small commandline tool (go) that accepts an incident id or JSON blob and emits a runbook to stdout or a file. Useful for SREs who prefer terminal workflows and for automation in runbooks-as-code. - diagnostics contextualizer: a module that collects top-N spans and error messages, applies configurable redaction rules (email, PII, long stack frames), and summarizes probable root-cause signals. - opt-in privacy flow: traces and logs are only attached when the incident has `attach_diagnostics: true` or when the user requests via Slack button. By default we provide only metadata and pointers to SLOs/dashboards. - tests: unit tests for CLI parsing, diagnostics obfuscation rules, and runbook templates; end-to-end integration test that exercises Slack flow (mocked). - docs: update docs/runbooks.md with examples and a short security note. Backwards compatibility: existing /triage and /runbook-short commands are unchanged; this new flow is additive. Checklist: - [x] CLI implementation and build script - [x] Slack command + REST endpoint - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Documentation updates - [x] Privacy/obfuscation review Notes and limitations: - The generated runbook is intentionally conservative (3 prioritized steps max) to avoid prescriptive automation. - Diagnostics attachments are limited to 10MB; larger payloads fall back to links. - This PR wires in a dependency on the slo-toolkit helper for SLO metadata lookup; that is a lightweight, vendored package.

review_comments: Arjun: This looks useful; two asks: (1) make redaction configurable via org policy, (2) please add a rate limit on /runbook to prevent abuse.
Maya: Addressed both. Added org-wide policy hook (ENV: REDACT_POLICY_URL) and token-bucket limiter keyed by team. See contextualizer.go and api/routes/runbook.go.
Elena: Security review: ensure we never leak full stack traces by default. Can you add a fallback that returns a pointer to logs when payloads exceed size?
Maya: Added 10MB cap and fallback link to log storage. Documented in docs/runbooks.md and tests cover the cap behavior.
Priya: Approved after minor nit on wording in CLI help text.

release_notes: Add oncall CLI and a Slack-integrated runbook generator. Generates short, privacy-aware runbooks and optional contextual diagnostics. Opt-in diagnostics attachment and SLO metadata integration.
